The search-external-sites agent was unable to search for Patrick Flynn's federal land patent, and here's why:

**Pennsylvania is not covered by the BLM General Land Office (GLO) database.** Pennsylvania is one of the original thirteen states, which means the federal government never distributed land there through the federal patent system. All land in Pennsylvania passed through the **state's own Land Office**, not the federal GLO — so the federal land-patent database holds nothing for Pennsylvania, and a search there would prove nothing either way.

**What to do instead:**

To find out whether Patrick Flynn received a land grant in Pennsylvania, the right sources are:

- **Pennsylvania State Archives** — the Pennsylvania Land Office records, which cover warrants, surveys, and patents issued by the Commonwealth.
- **County deed books** — deeds of sale and conveyance recorded in the county where Patrick Flynn lived.

If you'd like, I can ask the **research-plan** agent to add these Pennsylvania-specific land searches to your project's plan.

output.text_response:
Here is what the search-external-sites agent found and recommends:

---

**GenealogyBank Search — Patrick Flynn Obituary, Schuylkill County, PA**

A search entry (log_006) has been recorded for this search. The site may require a subscription or login.

**Open this search link:**
👉 [GenealogyBank – Patrick Flynn obituary, Schuylkill County, PA](https://www.genealogybank.com/explore/newspapers/all/usa/pennsylvania?q=Patrick+Flynn+obituary+Schuylkill)

**What to do:**
1. Open the link above on GenealogyBank.
2. Set the **date range to 1908** (and possibly into early 1909, the period around Patrick's death).
3. Look for a death notice or obituary for Patrick Flynn in a Schuylkill County paper — pay special attention to any "son of" language or survivor lists, which could identify his parents.
4. When done, **save the results page as a PDF** (Ctrl+P → Save as PDF on Windows) and upload it here so the agent can triage the hits.

**Alternative:** FamilySearch holds **Pennsylvania Death Certificates 1906–1968**, which may also yield information if GenealogyBank requires a subscription.

Once you upload the capture, the agent can go through the results and identify which entries look like the right Patrick Flynn.

items.description: Patrick Flynn's birthplace: Ireland (1850 and 1860 censuses) vs. Pennsylvania (1908 death certificate)
items.independence_analysis: The two census records (1850, 1860) are independent original sources with different enumerators. The death certificate is a third independent original source. However, the census informants are likely the same household member (Thomas Flynn or wife), so the two census assertions may share a single informant — potentially not fully independent for this fact.
items.weighing_analysis: The census records are contemporary recordings made near the time of Patrick's birth, while the death certificate was created 63 years later. The census informant was likely a household member with firsthand knowledge (primary or indeterminate), while the death certificate informant (son-in-law) is clearly secondary for birth facts. Two contemporary sources outweigh one later recollection by a secondary informant.
items.resolution_rationale: Ireland is accepted as the birthplace. The 1908 death certificate birthplace of 'Pennsylvania' is rejected as a likely error by the son-in-law informant, who may have confused Patrick's place of residence with his place of birth, or may not have known Patrick was born in Ireland before immigrating as a young child.

items.rationale: Confirm Patrick still in Thomas Flynn household in 1860. Strengthens parent-child identification.
Death certificate may name parents directly.
Thomas Flynn probate/will may name Patrick as son.

notes: this archive's URL carries no date filter — tell the user which date range to set in the site's own UI. The access classification is this class's default, NOT checked against this archive: if it turns out to need a subscription, say so rather than treating it as settled

items.description: Patrick Flynn's birthplace: Ireland (1850 and 1860 censuses) vs. Pennsylvania (1908 death certificate)

Two contemporary sources outweigh one later recollection by a secondary informant.
items.resolution_rationale: Ireland is accepted as the birthplace. output.text_response:
Here is what the search-external-sites agent found:

---

**Matricula Online (Browse Site)**

Matricula is a browse site — it does not support name searches — but it may hold the Ochtrup Catholic parish register.

**Direct link to start:**
👉 [https://data.matricula-online.eu/en/](https://data.matricula-online.eu/en/)

**How to browse for Wilhelm's 1836 marriage:**
1. Go to the Matricula front page and find **Ochtrup** in the places/dioceses list (Diocese of Münster / Bistum Münster, Kreis Steinfurt, Westphalia).
2. Open its parish page and select the **marriage register** (*Trauungen*, or a combined baptisms/marriages/deaths volume) covering 1836.
3. Page through the 1836 entries looking for **Wilhelm Kuhlmann**.
4. If you find the entry, save the page as a PDF (Ctrl+P → Save as PDF) and upload it here for extraction.

---

**FamilySearch Catalog Finding**

The Catholic parish register for Ochtrup (**"Kirchenbuch, 1667–1875"**) is on **film 876540** (Taufen, Heiraten, Tote 1804–1865), which covers 1836. It was filmed from the **Bistumsarchiv Münster**. However, it is **not available online** — it can only be viewed at a FamilySearch Center or affiliate library.

---

**Key Notes**
- **Civil records** for Ochtrup on FamilySearch begin in 1874, so they do not cover 1836.
- If Ochtrup is **not listed on Matricula**, the best path is to visit a FamilySearch Center to view film 876540, or contact the Bistumsarchiv Münster directly.
- Once you have an image or PDF, hand it to the record-structurer agent for extraction.

Here is the search link and instructions from the subagent:

---

**MyHeritage Search — Patrick Flynn, Pennsylvania Marriage (1865–1875)**

Open this prefilled search URL:

👉 [https://www.myheritage.com/research?s=1&formId=master&formMode=1&useTranslation=1&exactSearch=&p=1&action=query&view_mode=card&qname=Name+fn.Patrick+fnmo.1+ln.Flynn+lnmsrs.false&qevents-event1=Event+et.any+ep.Pennsylvania%2C+United+States+epmo.similar&qevents=List](https://www.myheritage.com/research?s=1&formId=master&formMode=1&useTranslation=1&exactSearch=&p=1&action=query&view_mode=card&qname=Name+fn.Patrick+fnmo.1+ln.Flynn+lnmsrs.false&qevents-event1=Event+et.any+ep.Pennsylvania%2C+United+States+epmo.similar&qevents=List)

**What to do:**
- On the results page, narrow by **event type = Marriage** and enter the year range **1865–1875** yourself (MyHeritage ranks rather than filters, so this is done manually).
- Look for a Patrick Flynn married in that window, roughly 20–30 years old at the time.
- **Note:** MyHeritage is not on file as one of your subscriptions (Ancestry is), so the page may prompt you to log in or show only a preview.
- When done, scroll the full results page, **save it as a PDF** (Ctrl+P → Save as PDF on Windows), and upload it here.

**Heads up:** FamilySearch also holds Pennsylvania Civil Marriages 1677–1950 and Compiled Marriages 1700–1900, which can be searched there as an alternative if MyHeritage hits a paywall.

Once you upload the PDF capture, the results will be triaged and the best matches identified.

items.description: Patrick Flynn's birthplace: Ireland (1850 and 1860 censuses) vs. Pennsylvania (1908 death certificate)
items.independence_analysis: The two census records (1850, 1860) are independent original sources with different enumerators. The death certificate is a third independent original source. However, the census informants are likely the same household member (Thomas Flynn or wife), so the two census assertions may share a single informant — potentially not fully independent for this fact.
items.weighing_analysis: The census records are contemporary recordings made near the time of Patrick's birth, while the death certificate was created 63 years later. The census informant was likely a household member with firsthand knowledge (primary or indeterminate), while the death certificate informant (son-in-law) is clearly secondary for birth facts. Two contemporary sources outweigh one later recollection by a secondary informant.
items.resolution_rationale: Ireland is accepted as the birthplace. The 1908 death certificate birthplace of 'Pennsylvania' is rejected as a likely error by the son-in-law informant, who may have confused Patrick's place of residence with his place of birth, or may not have known Patrick was born in Ireland before immigrating as a young child.

items.rationale: Confirm Patrick still in Thomas Flynn household in 1860. Strengthens parent-child identification.
Death certificate may name parents directly.
Thomas Flynn probate/will may name Patrick as son.

notes: this site ranks rather than filters — a year or place reorders the results toward your criteria without shrinking the count, so a large number of hits is expected and is not a failed search; marriage year and parent names cannot be expressed in the URL at all and must be entered in the site's own form
